At WWDC 2021, Apple announced support for storing driver's licenses in Apple Wallet on iPhone. Apple touted it at the time as the final step to "completely ditch your physical wallet."

Here's where Apple Wallet driver's license support is headed next...

Apple Wallet ID support

In the five years since Apple announced the feature, support has gradually expanded across the country. Currently, iPhone and Apple Watch users in 14 states and Puerto Rico can add their driver's license or state ID to Apple Wallet. You can see the full list here:

Where is it rolling out next? Here's what we know so far.

These seven states have confirmed they are working on Apple Wallet driver's license support, have been promoted by Apple as partners, or have appeared in Apple's code:

  • Kentucky (rolling out "summer" 2026)
  • North Carolina (rolling out early 2027)
  • Oklahoma (in the works, launch date TBD)
  • Utah (in the works, launch date TBD)
  • Virginia (in the works, launch date TBD)
  • Connecticut (status unknown, previously promoted by Apple as a partner)
  • Mississippi (status unknown, previously promoted by Apple as a partner)

On the other hand, the Secure Technology Alliance has been tracking the rollout of mobile driver's licenses across the country. Here are some states that have begun exploring mobile ID support through legislation or studies, but have not been mentioned by Apple:

  • Indiana
  • Vermont
  • New Jersey
  • Florida
  • South Carolina
  • Tennessee
  • Missouri
  • Nevada
  • Wyoming

Keep in mind that progress varies significantly from state to state. A state exploring or developing support for digital IDs doesn't necessarily mean it will eventually launch, let alone make it to Apple Wallet.

Wrap up

As you can see, Apple Wallet driver's license support rollout remains quite scattered across the country.

However, you don't have to wait for your state to support Apple Wallet digital IDs to try it out.

Apple launched a new "digital ID" feature last year powered by your US passport. While it's not your driver's license, it allows you to use your iPhone at TSA checkpoints at over 250 airports nationwide.

Do you store your ID or driver's license in Apple Wallet on your iPhone? Have you actually used it? Let us know in the comments.
